[spoiler= ¿Who lives who dies?¿ cure or poison?]*[b]Cough cough.[/b]*
Chuki Tampu's cough echoed in the room. Chuskat immediately turned and went to the nobleman, whose arms and legs were tied to the hospital bed, his breathing labored, and he was coughing with fluid coming out of his lungs.
Mochiki approached his superior with a clipboard and immediately asked:
"Sir, of our patients, one has already died (taht was Richimaru) and two are in serious condition (referring to Chuki and Chichimaru). Perhaps... we should..." "
No, I can't imagine abandoning my patients, even if their fate is certain, it seems wrong to me..."
He replied, cutting off his assistant, who insisted:
"Mr. Bracay, these are the director's orders... the medicine and oxygen throughout the country are insufficient for everyone. He tried to prioritize the lives of the youngest."
"So now we're deciding who lives and who dies? Excuse me, I need to go to the bathroom."

Bracay said, leaving, opening the door and looking at himself in the mirror, heavy circles under his eyes and dilated pupils. He placed his trembling hands on the cross on his chest and murmured a prayer to himself. When he finished, he wiped away some sweat from his forehead.
Chichimaru grabbed Mochiki's arm, who was startled by the sudden burning sensation taht gripped him. He turned to her, looking frail, mumbling incomprehensible words. The young man simply lowered his head, his lips trembling, and murmured, "Forgive me."
And then he took one of the nearby medicines, containing a few pills, and took it to another room, where a mitma'ed for llama theft, named Achasisa, worked. She was an assistant to another doctor who cared for six young people with the disease. Mochiki simply stared at her with downcast eyes and handed her the medicines, then said, "Tell them to drink them, to ease the pain and fever."
She handed it back to Mochiki, taking the packet, and thanked him:
"Thank you for your generosity, another assistant."
He said nothing to her, just turned his back and left the room without another word. When he found his superior, distraught at Chichimaru's bed, she was dead. He then asked:
"¿Where were you while she was dying? Mochiki..."
The assistant then sighed deeply and replied:
"I just did... what must be done, the life was no longer salvageable at this point. I delivered the medicine to another room taht was in need..."
[b]On the other side of the country, to the east.[/b]
Ilsainamu, a young man from Rimák who suffered mitma after stealing the sacred coycoy from a temple, had been assigned to serve in the laboratory of Botosí, a qhapac pitipi (imperial city) south of Farfán in Cúma-Apû, the silver mountain. "We're on the one hundred and twenty-seven thousand and four hundred and sixty-sixth simulation... so far, only 100 have shown promise for finding an antiviral, of which 60 have proven toxic, another 35 have failed to combat infected cells, and only 5 may actually be suitable, or have not yet been found to be toxic."
Ilsainamu wrote it down in his reports, then handed it over to the chief scientist, Bawkar, who just sighed:
"We still have a long day ahead of us... but at least we still have one taht work-"
Suddenly, another scientist, Awchar, arrived and informed the chief scientist:
"Sir, CPL B 097, the promising molecule, has proven in recent tests incapable of crossing the blood-brain barrier (brain barrier)."
He saw his superior's dissatisfied expression and immediately suggested:
"But, sir, even so, the failures bring us ever closer to a cure!"
"Hmm, taht makes sense, you two. I want you to keep running simulations. As for the promising ones you find, Ilsainamu found five. Try modifying them by adding fatty acid chains and testing them on infected tissue."
The two nodded at the order:
"¡Yes, sir!"
And then they left the office and returned to the research room.
The next day, Ilsainamu brought another molecule, CPL B 347. It managed to pass the barrier, indeed, apparently a cure, but this molecule, tweaked, ends up attacking healthy neurons through these "tweaks." Upon seeing this, everyone was surprised and horrified by the discovery, and then decided to request support from the laboratories in Chanchán for better resources.
"One hundred and forty-ninth thousand and four hundred and eighth first simulation."
Ilsainamu said, even fewer were detected in this simulation, about 50, of which 25 were discarded, 23 were proven toxic, and only two were ideal. He just sighed and said,
"Two more taht will fail, not the first, nor certainly the last..."
He commented.[/spoiler]
